personas.name: Renata Villalobos
personas.who: 38, room parent for a class of 24 and the person who ends up running every sign-up. She is the research's organizer: 5% of sessions, 100% of the adoption decision. Left SignUpGenius after a parent complained about the video ads on the sheet she'd sent.
personas.context: Kitchen table, 21:40, iPhone at 414px in one hand while the dishwasher runs. Ten minutes before she gives up for the night. She has the potluck list already written in Notes and wants to paste it.
personas.task: Build the Fall potluck sheet, ten spots with quantities, and get the link into the class WhatsApp before bed.
personas.verdict: She got there in about eight minutes and the finished sheet is genuinely better-looking than anything she's sent before. But she reopened the Manage panel eleven times, because it slams shut every single time she touches it, and she has no idea that fifty of the lines she pasted were thrown away.
delights: 'Copy nudge' produced a paste-ready message with no prompting: 'Still need a hand with “Fall potluck, Room 12”! Open spots: • Side or salad (3 needed) • Dessert (2 needed) … Grab one here (no account needed): <link>'. This is the research's #2 differentiator, shipped and working.
Pasting 'Main dish x3 / Side or salad x4 / Dessert x2' created three spots with the right capacities in 3.1 seconds. 'x', '×' and '(4)' all parse.
The share card is the first thing an owner sees: a 27px share code, Copy link, and a QR button, above everything else.

frictions.what: The Manage panel is a <details> rebuilt from scratch on every redraw with no `open` attribute (app.js:391). Measured: switching from 'One at a time' to 'Paste a list' sets details.open true → false. Adding spots does it too, after her 150-line paste the panel was closed (`open: false`), along with 102 full re-renders of <main> during the write.
frictions.whyItMatters: Every single owner action closes the console she is working in. Choosing the input mode, adding one spot, renaming the sheet, and, because the redraw is driven by Firestore snapshots, any participant claiming a spot anywhere in the world while she types. Setup is the make-or-break minute the research names ('sheet creation must be under 60 seconds with no wizard'), and the app spends it re-collapsing itself.

frictions.what: She pasted 150 shift lines. 100 spots were created and the toast said '100 spots added'. helpers.js:36 breaks the parse loop at 100 and returns quietly; nothing anywhere reports the 50 discarded lines.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the exact betrayal the research puts at the centre of the category, a cap discovered after the work is done, reported as a success. Fifty shifts do not exist and she has no reason to look.

frictions.what: Second paste onto a sheet that already had 60 spots: the cap check at app.js:520 fires, toasts 'Sheets max out at 100 spots', adds nothing, and then app.js:427 clears the textarea anyway, because addSlotsChecked returns normally instead of throwing. Measured: 50 typed lines, 0 characters left in the box.
frictions.whyItMatters: She is told to split into a second sheet, and the thing she would paste into the second sheet has just been deleted from in front of her. Same at app.js:418 for a single label.

frictions.what: Saving a slot edit produces nothing at all. Measured: renaming 'Week 1 snack' → 'Week 1 snack (renamed)' fired zero toasts; the dialog just closes (app.js:610). Same for Title & details, that one at least toasts 'Saved'.
frictions.whyItMatters: sws-ui.js ships SWS.saved() precisely for this and index.html loads it; app.js calls it zero times. Silence after a save is how a tired organizer ends up saving twice.

frictions.what: 'Your sheets' on the home screen lists title, share code and an Open button and nothing else (app.js:147-151). No fill count, no date, no duplicate, no delete, no archive.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research names recurring coordination, meal trains, monthly snack rotas, weekly nursery shifts, as the real usage pattern, with 'duplicate for next month' as the differentiator. Next month she will build the same sheet again by hand, and the only way to delete last month's is to open it and dig through Manage.

personas.name: Dolores Weatherstone
personas.who: 71, grandmother, macular changes plus varifocals. Confident with her iPad, wary of anything that looks like software. Got the meal-train link forwarded twice. This is the comfort-panel persona.
personas.context: Sitting room, mid-morning, iPad in portrait at 414 CSS px propped on a cushion, bright window behind her, reading glasses on the arm of the chair. No time pressure, low patience.
personas.task: Take Tuesday's dinner slot on a hospice sitting rota, then change her mind and swap to Monday.
personas.verdict: She claimed Tuesday and she liked the page. She could not release it. The ✕ that gives a spot back measured 16 × 19 pixels, and even after she turned the text up to Largest it was 22 × 29, still the smallest thing on the screen and still under the 44px floor the design system sets.
delights: She found the gear in the header unprompted, opened it, and set Text size to Largest. It worked properly: root font 16px → 24px, slot labels 16px → 24px, the whole layout scaled in proportion, and page overflow stayed at exactly 0px at 414px AND at 320px. axe with the panel open: zero violations. The permanent tick slot meant she could see which option was on.
The claim dialog at Largest is 381 × 506 with a 343 × 66 'Claim it' button, fully inside the viewport, nothing clipped.
Her own claim is marked '(you)' and tinted with a distinct --mine background plus an accent border, not colour alone, and it survives dark mode.

frictions.what: The release control is `.chip button` (index.html:1276), border:0, background:none, padding:0 2px, font-size:.9rem. Measured 16 × 19px at default and 22 × 29px at Largest text. Its only visible form is a ✕ glyph inside the name pill.
frictions.whyItMatters: 'Un-claim or edit your own entry from the same link' is on the research's table-stakes list, every credible tool in the category has it. Here it exists and is effectively unhittable, and a miss lands on the chip, which does nothing, so she tapped four times and concluded she was stuck with Tuesday.

frictions.what: 'Claim this spot' is `.btn primary small` (app.js:331), and `.btn.small` is a hardcoded `min-height:36px` (index.html:607). Measured 123 × 36px at Default text, 137 × 36 at Large, 173 × 36 at Largest, the height never moves while the label inside grows from 13px to 19.5px.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the one button 95% of sessions exist to press, and it is the only control on the page that refuses to grow with her text setting. The design system's rule is explicit: --tap is floored at 44px and scales with --ui-scale precisely because someone turning the text up is doing it for eyesight or tremor.

frictions.what: The availability number, '2 of 4', 'Full', is `.slot .count` at 0.82rem (index.html:1281), measured 13.12px. 'Full' renders in --pos green, the same green the system uses for success.
frictions.whyItMatters: The single fact she came for is set in the smallest type on the page, below the system's 15px instructional floor, and 'Full' being green reads as good news when it is the opposite.

frictions.what: A 'Sign in' button sits in the header on the participant view (index.html:1337). At 414px the header is 112px tall across four rows, and 'Sign in' is on its own line directly under the title.
frictions.whyItMatters: The page's whole promise is that she does not need an account, and the most button-shaped thing above the fold says Sign in. She asked whether she had to.

personas.name: Marcus Oyelaran
personas.who: 44, dad of two, in the school pickup line. Got the link in a group text at 14:58. Has never heard of the app and has about fifteen seconds of attention before the gate opens.
personas.context: Standing, one thumb, phone at 414px, bright afternoon sun, car keys in the other hand. Arrives mildly suspicious of an unsolicited link.
personas.task: Take the last dessert slot before someone else does.
personas.verdict: He lost the race, which is fine, but he lost it the way the category is hated for. He tapped 'Claim it', the dialog vanished in 53ms with no spinner, and about a second later a toast told him it didn't go through. His typed note was gone and nothing offered him another spot.
delights: Cold open of the shared link to the first slot painted: 554ms on a 5-slot sheet, 1,035ms on a 60-slot one. No layout shift after paint, no cookie banner, no interstitial, no install bar, the research's second complaint, answered.

The footer on a shared sheet reads 'Made with Signup Sheets, free, no ads. Start yours' (app.js:99-101) instead of the studio colophon. The stance is on the participant-facing sheet, exactly as the research asks.
Claiming took one tap, one field and a second tap. No account, no email, no verification, and the app remembers his name in localStorage ('ss-myname') for next time.

frictions.what: app.js:594 closes the dialog BEFORE awaiting the write (`closeDlg($('nameDlg')); … await D.claimSlot(…)`). Measured: dialog gone in 53ms; the failure toast arrives after the round trip. On the loser's screen the note field still holds 'tiramisu, my mother's recipe', inside a dialog that is closed and will be blanked the next time it opens (app.js:341 sets noteInput to '').
frictions.whyItMatters: The research quotes this exact moment as the most humiliating in the category: 'by the time I have gotten to the end, another person has taken that spot', and names 'never lose typed input on a claim collision' as a differentiator. His name survives by accident, via localStorage. His note does not.

frictions.what: The failure message is 'That didn't go through, the spot may have just filled, or the sheet is locked.' (app.js:56). No nearest-open-slot offer; the sheet simply redraws with someone else's name in the pill.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's fix is one tap: 'keep the name in the field, say plainly what happened, and offer the nearest still-open slot as a single tap.' Two of the three are there; the tap is not, and 'or the sheet is locked' makes a clear event ambiguous.

frictions.what: Nothing happens visually between the tap and the answer. The dialog closes, the button does not disable, no spinner, no optimistic row.
frictions.whyItMatters: On a good connection the gap is a few hundred milliseconds. In a pickup line on one bar it is seconds of a page that looks like it ignored him, which is when people tap again or close the tab.

frictions.what: On a 60-slot conference sheet the page is 6,980px tall with 60 identical 'Claim this spot' buttons and no filter. Measured: no 'show only open', no 'hide full', no still-needed sentence, the only summary is a progress bar and '0 of 60 spots filled'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Capterra, quoted in the research: 'the layout often times may get a little annoying when scrolling down to find open time slots.' The research asks for availability answerable in under two seconds without scrolling; here it takes seven screenfuls.

personas.name: Jules Kenny
personas.who: 31, developer with RSI. Drives everything from the keyboard, uses a trackball sparingly and never for repeated clicking. Helping his partner set up the church nursery rota.
personas.context: Desk, 1280px window, hands on the keyboard only, no time pressure and high standards.
personas.task: Build a repeating sheet: every Tuesday and Thursday from September to November, two volunteers per date.
personas.verdict: Could not do it at all. The 'Repeating dates' generator is unreachable from the keyboard because the weekday checkboxes are display:none, so there is no way to say which days. He fell back to typing 26 dates by hand into the bulk box.
delights: The participant path is genuinely keyboard-clean: Tab order runs brand → comfort settings → tip jar → Sign in → each 'Claim this spot' → the notes fields. Enter opens the claim dialog, focus lands on #nameInput automatically, Enter submits, and the ✕ release is a real focusable button.
Escape closes every dialog, and nothing is focus-trapped.
Zero console errors across every run, cold loads, 100-spot pastes, races, offline claims, deletions. Not one.

frictions.what: `.wkdays input{display:none}` at index.html:1307. Measured: 7 checkboxes, computed display 'none', bounding box 0×0, 0 of 7 present in the focusable set. Tabbing from the 'From' date field never reaches them.
frictions.whyItMatters: WCAG 2.1.1 failure on a whole feature. The design system says this in so many words two hundred lines above, in a comment about the comfort panel's own radios: 'display:none or visibility:hidden would make the group unreachable by keyboard, which is the exact defect the Pill Schedule audit found in the shipped app.' The app then does it anyway.

frictions.what: The theme dots (app.js:465-476) are 34 × 34px buttons whose entire content is a background colour, named 'blue theme', 'green theme' and so on.
frictions.whyItMatters: Under the 44px floor, and the state is carried by a box-shadow ring with no aria-pressed. A screen reader is told there are five buttons named after colours and never which one is on.

frictions.what: After a successful claim, activeElement is <body> (measured). The dialog is closed by app.js:594 and focus is never returned to the 'Claim this spot' button that opened it. Same after Escape on the auth dialog.
frictions.whyItMatters: On a 60-slot sheet, taking two slots means tabbing from the top of the document twice, 4 chrome stops plus up to 60 buttons.

frictions.what: Four native confirm() dialogs (app.js:455 add N dated spots, :492 rotate link, :498 delete sheet, :615 delete a spot and its signups) and zero undo. window.SWS is present with {toast, undo, hideToast, saved}, app.js references it zero times.
frictions.whyItMatters: The portfolio's stated answer to destructive actions is undo, not confirm; the runtime is loaded on this page and untouched. Deleting a spot that already has signups is permanent, silent to the people who signed up, and one tap away behind a browser alert.

personas.name: Ana Ruiz
personas.who: 56, deacon at a small church, coordinates meal trains for families after a death or a diagnosis. Not technical; deeply attuned to tone. The research's warning case: the same sheet format runs funeral receptions and hospice shifts.
personas.context: Parish office desktop at 1280px in the morning, then her phone in the evening. She will print the sheet and put it on the noticeboard because half the congregation is over seventy.
personas.task: Run a two-week meal train for a bereaved family, print a copy for the foyer, and keep the tone right.
personas.verdict: The sheet itself is warm and dignified and the print is the best she has seen from a free tool. Then she opened the colour picker, found it already showing blue as her choice, tapped it, and got a page with an orange button and a blue progress bar. She turned it back off, except there is no 'off'.
delights: The printed sheet is a real sign-up sheet: title, details line, 'x of y spots filled', each spot with its claimed names, and a blank pill '________________' printed for every unclaimed place. Header, Manage, share card, all buttons and the colophon are correctly hidden. One page for a five-spot sheet. This is the research's 'compete with paper rather than against it', shipped.
The default marigold palette is warm without being celebratory, no confetti, no clip-art, no theme wallpaper. It carries a bereavement meal train without a wince.
Locking the sheet works end to end: the participant sees 'This sheet is locked by the organizer, read-only for now', all claim buttons disappear, and the notes composer is withdrawn.

frictions.what: applyTheme() (app.js:219-223) sets only `--accent` inline on <html>. Measured after choosing blue: --accent #2563eb, but --accent-fill still #f7933c, --focus still #a95a00, --accent-deep still marigold. The primary button stays orange (rgb(247,147,60)), links stay warm brown, and only the fill bar and the weekday chips turn blue.
frictions.whyItMatters: The result is not a blue sheet, it is a broken one, and it propagates to every participant who opens the link. Worse, the research is explicit that an organizer-selectable theme system is 'precisely what makes their pages look dated and untrustworthy', and that SaaS blue is the single hue to avoid. This ships both.

frictions.what: The picker shows blue as already selected on a sheet that has no theme at all, `(s.theme || 'blue') === key` at app.js:469, while applyTheme leaves the marigold skin in place when settings.theme is absent. Measured: `--accent` inline = '' (skin default) while the blue dot carries `.sel`. There is also no way back to 'no theme'.
frictions.whyItMatters: The control lies about the current state, and once touched it cannot be untouched. She had to ask the organizer of a bereavement sheet to live with whatever she picked.

frictions.what: Deleting a spot that people had already signed up for: a native confirm ('Delete this spot and its 1 signup(s)?'), then nothing. Measured on the participant's screen: the spot silently vanishes from the list and their stale toast still reads 'You're in, Week 1 snack'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Someone who committed to bring Tuesday's dinner to a grieving family is quietly un-committed and told nothing. There is no undo for Ana either.

frictions.what: The printed sheet carries no date, no share code, no link and no QR. It also prints the 'you run this' badge and the Extras placeholder quote '“I'll also bring lemonade!”, anything that isn't a listed spot goes here.' as if it were content.
frictions.whyItMatters: The whole reason to print is the noticeboard, and the noticeboard copy is a dead end, nobody who reads it can get to the live sheet. The lemonade line on a bereavement meal train is the tonal misfire the research warns about, printed in ink.

personas.name: Tobias Frei
personas.who: 36, blind, VoiceOver on iOS. Books his own parent-teacher slots. Chose this link over the school's usual tool because a friend said it had no ads.
personas.context: Sofa, evening, iPhone at 414px with VoiceOver, headphones on. Patient, but he will leave a page that talks over itself.
personas.task: Find and book a 10-minute conference slot on a 60-slot sheet.
personas.verdict: He booked one. He also heard the entire page read to him seventy-three times in the first six seconds, because <main> is a live region and every one of the sixty slot listeners redraws it.
delights: axe against the fully rendered participant board, and against the owner board, and with the comfort panel open: zero violations in all three. Every input has a real label or aria-label; the ✎ and ✕ buttons carry aria-labels; the code box is labelled 'Sheet code'.
Every user string reaches the DOM through textContent (the el() helper at app.js:19). '<script>alert(1)</script>' as a spot label rendered as literal text with zero injected script nodes.
'Full' vs '3 of 4' is real text, not a colour or an icon, so the state of every slot is readable.

frictions.what: index.html:1339 is `<main id="view" aria-live="polite">`, and drawBoard() (app.js:225-234) calls replaceChildren() on it. Measured on a 60-slot sheet: 3,491 characters inside the live region, 73 full replacements in the six seconds after load, 6 more for a single claim, 102 during one bulk add. Each slot gets its own onSnapshot listener that calls drawBoard (app.js:212-213).
frictions.whyItMatters: The app asks a screen reader to re-announce the whole sheet dozens of times on load and again whenever anyone, anywhere, claims anything. There is no aria-atomic and no dedicated status region, so the things worth announcing, 'you're in', 'that spot just filled', arrive buried in a re-read of the entire page.

frictions.what: The pending-note badge is appended straight after the body text with only a CSS margin (app.js:354). innerText reads 'Ana Ruiz: I will also bring lemonade and cupsawaiting approval'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Sighted users see a 6px gap and a pill. He hears one run-on word. Status that decides whether a note is visible to anyone should not be glued to the sentence.

frictions.what: None of the five <dialog> elements carries aria-labelledby (measured: authDlg, nameDlg, createDlg, slotDlg, qrDlg all null), even though #nameDlgTitle already has an id. The QR canvas has no role, no aria-label and no text alternative.
frictions.whyItMatters: A dialog announces itself as 'dialog' with no name. The QR dialog announces a heading and then silence where the code is, and the code is the only content.

frictions.what: No skip link, despite .skip being styled in the base at index.html:858 and hidden in print at :1214. The header has four focusable controls before the content on every load.
frictions.whyItMatters: Four stops before the sheet, every time, on a page whose whole content is a list of buttons.

worksWell: The participant path is fast, clean and honest. 554ms to first slot on a small sheet, 1,035ms on a 60-slot one; one tap to a dialog, one field, one tap to claim; the name is remembered locally; zero console errors in any run; zero axe violations on the fully rendered board.

Layout is unbreakable. Page overflow measured exactly 0px in every combination tried: 320px, 414px, 1280px, Largest text at both phone widths, roomy + easier reading + warmth 3, dark mode, and a 100-spot sheet. Not one offending element anywhere.

The stance is on the shared sheet, not just the marketing page, the colophon on a participant's view is rewritten to 'Made with Signup Sheets, free, no ads. Start yours'. That is the research's single biggest wedge against SignUpGenius, shipped where it counts.
'Copy nudge' works and is good: a paste-ready group-chat message listing only the open spots with counts and the link. Nobody in the category does this well.
Print is a real sign-up sheet. Blank '________________' pills for every unclaimed place, claimed names filled in, chrome and buttons correctly hidden, one page for a five-spot sheet.

Text safety is total. Every user string goes through textContent; script and img payloads render as literal text with zero injected nodes; no NaN, Infinity, undefined or [object Object] reached the screen under any numeric input.

The comfort panel is faultless and it helps: opens from the header, focus moves inside, axe clean, Largest takes the root from 16px to 24px, and slot labels, chips, dialogs and the notes composer all scale with it. Dark mode is correct on every app-layer colour.

The realtime model is honest about failure. Offline shows a banner and the claim still applies locally and syncs on reconnect; a rotated code gives 'That sheet doesn't exist, the code may have been rotated by the organizer'; approval-required notes round-trip correctly between participant and owner.
hurts: The owner's Manage panel closes on every interaction, mode switch, add, save, and also whenever any participant claims anything, because it is rebuilt without its open state on every Firestore snapshot.
Silent data loss on the way in: a 150-line paste creates 100 spots and toasts '100 spots added'; a paste that would breach the cap is rejected and the textarea is cleared anyway.
'Claim this spot' is 36px tall at every text setting, and the release ✕ is 16 × 19px. The two verbs the product exists for are the two smallest targets on the page.
The claim dialog closes before the write resolves, so a lost race destroys the typed note, shows no progress in between, and offers no other slot.
<main> is a live region that gets fully replaced 73 times on a 60-slot cold load and again on every remote change, which also wipes any half-typed note and throws focus to <body>.
The 'Repeating dates' generator is keyboard-unusable: its weekday checkboxes are display:none, 0 of 7 focusable.
The colour picker is half-wired (only --accent moves), lies about the current selection, has no off switch, and its default choice is the exact SaaS blue the research says to avoid.
No undo anywhere; four native confirm() dialogs instead, while window.SWS.undo sits loaded and unused. Deleting a spot with signups tells the signed-up nobody.
One participant claimed 8 of 8 spots with no cap, no warning and no notice to the organizer.
There is no way to edit a claim, only remove and re-add. data.js:259 exports renameClaim() and nothing calls it.
A deleted sheet keeps rendering: watchBoard returns null, drawBoard early-returns, and the participant is left with a live-looking board whose claim button fails.
Availability is set in the smallest type on the page (13.12px), and 'Full' is rendered in success green.
mostWantedNext: Stop rebuilding the world: keep the Manage panel's open state and the addMode across redraws, and patch the slot list instead of replacing <main>, that one change fixes the collapsing panel, the wiped note field, the lost focus and most of the screen-reader noise at once.
Report what was dropped. 'Added 100 to 50 more lines were not imported' and never clear a textarea whose contents were not accepted.
Raise 'Claim this spot' and the release ✕ to var(--tap), and give the release a word ('Give it back') rather than a 16px glyph.
Hold the claim dialog open until the write resolves, show progress on the button, and on a collision keep the note, say 'that one just filled', and offer the nearest open spot as one tap.
Per-person claim cap in Settings ('anyone may take up to N'), which the rules layer can enforce the same way it enforces capacity.
Undo via SWS.undo on all four confirm() paths, plus a note to the affected participants when a spot they hold is deleted.
Either finish the theme system (drive --accent-fill, --accent-deep, --focus and --accent-soft from the choice, add a 'default' option) or delete it, which is what the research recommends.
An 'open spots only' toggle and a still-needed sentence at the top, 'Still needed: 3 salads, 2 desserts, someone to bring ice', instead of only a progress bar.
Put the share code and a QR on the printed sheet, drop the 'you run this' badge and the empty-state lemonade line from print, and add a date.
An .ics download at the moment of claiming, the research's named answer to reminder emails and currently the most visible gap in the feature set.
Let people edit a claim, not just delete it, renameClaim() is already written and tested at the data layer.

scenarios.name: The standard battery (node design/stress.mjs signup-sheets)
scenarios.method: Ran the shipped battery unmodified: layout at 320/414/1280 and at largest-text and roomy, touch targets, hostile text and injection, numeric edges, 30 rapid clicks, 200 bulk adds, reload persistence, corrupt localStorage, keyboard reachability, axe after interaction, print, console errors.
scenarios.result: 0 hard failures. Layout clean at all five sizes. Touch targets: only a#brandLink at 134×26. Hostile text: 0 injected imgs, title not hijacked, no poison on screen. Keyboard: 9 focusable, 0 unreachable, 0 unnamed, 0 placeholder-only. axe: clean. Console: silent. BUT the battery never left the home screen, creating a sheet needs Firebase auth, so 'boots with corrupt storage' reported 'no app storage key to corrupt' and 'bulk: 200 rapid adds' reported 0 nodes. Everything below was run against the real app driven through local Firebase emulators (auth 9099, firestore 8081, project demo-signup) with firebase-config.js swapped at the network layer.
scenarios.defect: The standard battery is structurally blind to this app: 100% of its product surface sits behind a share code and an auth round trip.

scenarios.name: Owner console stability, does the Manage panel survive its own use?
scenarios.method: Created a sheet, opened <details class="manage">, read details.open, clicked the 'Paste a list' segment, read details.open again. Then pasted 150 lines and re-read. Counted full replacements of #view with a MutationObserver.
scenarios.result: open true → false on the mode switch. After the 150-line add: open false, and 102 full replaceChildren() of <main> during the write. The panel is created fresh by app.js:391 with no open attribute, and every Firestore snapshot calls drawBoard().
scenarios.defect: Every owner action, and every remote claim by anyone, closes the panel the owner is working in and destroys everything typed in it.

scenarios.name: Bulk paste past the cap
scenarios.method: Pasted 150 lines into an empty sheet; then pasted 50 lines onto a sheet that already held 60; then added one label to a sheet holding 100. Captured every toast via a MutationObserver on #toast.
scenarios.result: 150 lines → exactly 100 slots, one toast: '100 spots added'. 50 lines onto 60 → 0 added, toast 'Sheets max out at 100 spots, split into a second sheet if you need more.', and the textarea measured 0 characters afterwards. 1 label onto 100 → same toast, label field also cleared. helpers.js:36 breaks the parse at 100; app.js:520 returns rather than throws, so app.js:418/427 clear the field regardless.
scenarios.defect: 50 pasted lines discarded and reported as success; a rejected paste is deleted from the box the user would need to copy it out of.

scenarios.name: Two people racing for the last spot
scenarios.method: Two independent browser contexts on a one-capacity sheet. Both opened the claim dialog, both typed a name and a note, then both pressed 'Claim it' inside the same tick. Recorded the toast, dialog state, retained field values and the offer made afterwards.
scenarios.result: Winner: 'You're in, The last dessert'. Loser: dialog closed 53ms after the tap, toast 'That didn't go through, the spot may have just filled, or the sheet is locked.', slot redrew showing the winner's name. Loser's #nameInput and #noteInput still held their text, inside a closed dialog that app.js:341 blanks the note of on next open. 0 alternative slots offered. app.js:594 closes the dialog before awaiting the write.
scenarios.defect: The typed note is lost and the recovery tap the research asks for does not exist. The name survives only because saveName() ran before the attempt.

scenarios.name: Touch-target geometry across every comfort setting
scenarios.method: Measured the two verbs of the product at Default, Large and Largest text, at 414px and 320px, and compared against the --tap floor.
scenarios.result: 'Claim this spot': 123×36 @13px (default), 137×36 @14.95px (Large), 173×36 @19.5px (Largest), the height is constant because .btn.small hardcodes min-height:36px at index.html:607. Release ✕ (.chip button, index.html:1276): 16×19 default, 22×29 at Largest. Also under 44px: theme dots 34×34, ✎ edit slot 37×36, seg buttons 38, #authBtn 36, .wkdays label 33.
scenarios.defect: The primary action never grows with the text setting, and the un-claim action is a 16px glyph.

scenarios.name: Live-region volume on a realistic sheet
scenarios.method: Built a 60-slot conference sheet, cold-opened it as a participant, and counted childList replacements of <main id="view" aria-live="polite"> with a MutationObserver installed before load.
scenarios.result: 1,035ms to the first slot painted. 73 full replacements of the live region in the following 6 seconds; 3,491 characters inside it; 6 more replacements for one claim. Each slot gets its own onSnapshot at app.js:212, and every callback calls drawBoard(). No aria-atomic, no dedicated status region.
scenarios.defect: A screen reader is asked to re-read the whole sheet 73 times on load and again on every remote change.

scenarios.name: A remote change while a participant is typing
scenarios.method: Participant typed a name and a 29-character note into the Extras composer, put the caret mid-string, then the owner renamed an unrelated slot from another context. Read the field values and activeElement afterwards.
scenarios.result: Before: ['Half-typed Name', 'I will also bring a lemon dri']. After: ['Priya Raman', ''], the note is gone and the name field has been re-seeded from localStorage. activeElement: BODY.
scenarios.defect: Any claim by anyone, anywhere, deletes what the current user is typing and takes their focus.

scenarios.name: Keyboard reach into the repeating-dates generator
scenarios.method: Enumerated the focusable set on the owner console with 'Repeating dates' selected, intersected it with .wkdays input, and tabbed six stops from the 'From' date field.
scenarios.result: 7 weekday checkboxes, computed display 'none', bounding boxes 0×0, 0 of 7 in the focusable set. Tab never leaves the date inputs. index.html:1307 is `.wkdays input{display:none}`.
scenarios.defect: A whole feature is unreachable without a pointer, WCAG 2.1.1, and the design system warns against this exact pattern in its own comments.

scenarios.name: Layout under every comfort setting, on a real board
scenarios.method: Seeded sws.prefs before load in separate contexts and measured document overflow plus every element extending past the viewport: 414px + Largest + High contrast, 320px + Largest, 414px + roomy + easier reading + warmth 3, dark mode, and a 100-spot sheet at 414px.
scenarios.result: Overflow 0px in all five, offenders [] in all five. At Largest the root goes 16px → 24px and slot labels, chips (37px tall), the claim dialog (381×506, fits) and the 343×66 'Claim it' button all scale. Scroll to the bottom of a 6,980px 60-slot page: 0ms.

scenarios.name: Comfort panel driven for real from the participant view
scenarios.method: Opened #swsPrefsBtn on a shared sheet, ran axe with the panel open, selected Largest then Large by clicking the real radios, closed it, and re-measured the board.
scenarios.result: Panel opens, focus moves inside, axe returns 0 violations. Picking Largest writes data-text="xxl" and root 24px; picking Large writes 'l' and 18.4px, and the board follows immediately with overflow still 0. Settings persist across navigation via the sws.prefs key.
scenarios.defect: The panel has no defect. What it cannot reach is the 36px claim button and the 16px release ✕, which are pinned in the app layer.

scenarios.name: One participant taking everything
scenarios.method: Single anonymous context, claimed every open slot on an 8-spot snack rota in sequence, then searched the rendered page for any cap or warning language.
scenarios.result: 8 of 8 claimed. 8 .chip.mine pills. No warning, no cap, no notice to the organizer. All eight remove buttons carry the identical accessible name 'Remove Greedy Greg from this spot' with no slot in the label.
scenarios.defect: No per-person claim cap, which the research lists as table stakes ('you may take up to 2, so one eager parent doesn't silently take everything').

scenarios.name: Destructive owner actions
scenarios.method: Renamed a slot, set its capacity below its claim count, deleted a slot holding a signup, rotated the code, and deleted a whole sheet, each with a live participant context watching. Captured every toast and every native dialog message.
scenarios.result: Slot rename: 0 toasts, dialog just closes. Capacity '0' on a slot with 1 claim: parseInt('0')||1 clamps to 1 with no message, and the slot flips to 'Full'. Delete a spot with a signup: confirm 'Delete this spot and its 1 signup(s)?', no undo, no toast, and on the participant's screen the spot silently disappears while their stale toast still reads 'You're in, Week 1 snack'. Rotate: participant keeps working until reload, then gets the correct 'That sheet doesn't exist' card. window.SWS = {toast, undo, hideToast, saved} is loaded and called zero times by app.js.
scenarios.defect: No confirmation on save, no undo on anything, and no notice to the people whose commitment was deleted.

scenarios.name: Deleting a sheet out from under a live participant
scenarios.method: Owner deleted the board while a participant had it open; then the participant pressed 'Claim this spot'.
scenarios.result: The participant's page kept rendering the full board, title, spots, claim buttons, share card, indefinitely. watchBoard's callback passes null (data.js:121), drawBoard() early-returns at app.js:226 and leaves the stale DOM in place. Clicking Claim produced 'That didn't go through, the spot may have just filled, or the sheet is locked.' No console errors.
scenarios.defect: A deleted sheet keeps advertising itself as live, and the only feedback is a message about the wrong cause.

scenarios.name: The theme picker
scenarios.method: Read the computed tokens before and after choosing each dot, then loaded the sheet fresh in a participant context and screenshotted it.
scenarios.result: Before any choice: --accent #c06700 (skin), no inline override, yet the 'blue theme' dot already carries .sel, because app.js:469 defaults to 'blue'. After choosing blue: --accent inline #2563eb, but --accent-fill stays #f7933c, --focus #a95a00, --accent-deep unchanged. Screenshot confirms an orange-button page with one blue progress bar. Contrast of .wkdays label:has(input:checked), which pairs --accent with --accent-ink at 12.8px: marigold 4.69:1, amber 3.79:1, blue 3.69:1, green 3.46:1, plum 3.34:1, slate 2.51:1. There is no 'no theme' option.

scenarios.name: Print, with real claims on the sheet
scenarios.method: emulateMedia({media:'print'}) at A4, then page.pdf(), then read the generated PDF.
scenarios.result: One page. header.app, details.manage, .btn, .noprint, #toast and footer.colophon all correctly hidden; the share card and every remove ✕ gone; 9 blank '________________' chips printed for the 9 unclaimed places; names and notes intact. Missing from the paper: the date, the share code, the URL, any QR. Present and unwanted: the 'you run this' badge and the Extras empty-state line '“I'll also bring lemonade!”, anything that isn't a listed spot goes here.' Blank pills measure ~115px wide, short for a handwritten name. (CJK names printed as tofu, but this container has 0 Japanese fonts installed, that is the environment, not the app, and it is not counted as a defect.)

scenarios.name: QR code
scenarios.method: Opened the QR dialog, read the canvas pixels for module extent and quiet zone, exported the PNG and inspected it.
scenarios.result: 300×300 canvas, module block 34→264 (230px), quiet zone 34/34/36/36px, 26,558 dark pixels, scannable. The dialog's only control is 'Close', no download, no save, no print. The canvas has no role, no aria-label and no text alternative. #qrBox forces a white background so it survives dark mode.

scenarios.name: Bulk-paste parsing and capacity edges
scenarios.method: Pasted 12 deliberately awkward lines and separately added spots with capacity '0', '-5', '1e9', '0.5', 'abc', '' and '999999'. Scanned the whole page for NaN/Infinity/undefined/[object Object].
scenarios.result: 'Main dish x3'→3, 'Dessert ×2'→2, 'Salad (4)'→4, 'Table for 6'→1 (correctly not a multiplier), 'Bring 2 dozen cookies x2'→2, 'Chairs x0'→1, 'Ice x1000'→label kept whole, capacity 1 (regex is \d{1,3}), 'Volunteers x999'→999, '<script>alert(1)</script> x2'→literal text, 0 script nodes. Two lines vanished with no report: a whitespace-only line and 'x5' (label empties after the multiplier is stripped). Capacity: 0→1, -5→1, 1e9→1, 0.5→1, abc→1, empty→1, 999999→999, all silently. No poison text anywhere.
scenarios.defect: Silent substitution of typed numbers and silent dropping of unparseable lines; 'Ice x1000' behaves differently from 'Ice x100' with no explanation.

scenarios.name: Offline claim and reconnect
scenarios.method: Set the participant context offline, dispatched the offline event, claimed a spot, then went back online.
scenarios.result: Banner appears: 'You're offline, you can read the sheet; claims will sync when you're back.' The claim applies optimistically from Firestore's local cache, the row shows 'Ola Okafor (you)' immediately, but the success toast is empty, because app.js:596 awaits batch.commit() which does not resolve until the server acks. On reconnect the toast finally fires 'You're in, Bring the ice'. No errors, no duplicate write.
scenarios.defect: The confirmation arrives minutes late or not at all; the only offline feedback is the row quietly changing.

scenarios.name: Approval mode, rotated codes and mistyped codes
scenarios.method: Turned on 'Require my approval', posted a note as a participant, read both views; rotated a live code; opened #/b/ZZZZZZ; typed 'abc' into the code box.
scenarios.result: Approval round-trips correctly: participant sees their own pending note with an 'awaiting approval' badge and a toast 'Added, the organizer will approve it shortly'; the owner sees it with a ✓ approve button. innerText reads 'cupsawaiting approval', the badge is glued to the body text with only a CSS margin (app.js:354). Rotation and a bogus code both land on 'That sheet doesn't exist, the code may have been rotated by the organizer.' A short code toasts 'Codes are 6 letters/numbers, check the link you were sent'.
scenarios.defect: A stranger who mistypes a code is told about an organizer rotating it, which explains nothing; and the pending badge reads as one word to assistive tech.

scenarios.name: Dialog semantics, focus and the sign-in gate
scenarios.method: Enumerated all five <dialog> elements, opened each, read activeElement on open and after Escape, and walked the create-a-sheet path while signed out.

Focus on open: nameDlg→#nameInput, createDlg→#createTitle, slotDlg→#slotLabel, qrDlg→#qrClose, authDlg→#googleBtn, all sensible. audit.purpose: The portfolio's one networked app. An organizer signs in (Google or an email link), creates a sheet, adds spots, one at a time, pasted as a list with 'x3' multipliers, or generated across a date range and weekday set, and shares a 6-character code, a link, a QR or a paste-ready 'nudge' message. Anyone with the link claims a spot with a name and an optional note; participants are Firebase anonymous users, so their uid is the claim token that lets them release their own spot later on the same device, with no account. Owners can lock the sheet, require approval for free-text notes, recolour it, rotate the code (killing the old link instantly) and delete it. Data lives in Firestore under boards/{id} with slots, claims and entries subcollections, and a separate codes/{CODE} → boardId map so a leaked code exposes only an opaque id; firestore.rules is the real product, batch-coupling every participant write to a counter so capacity, one-claim-per-person and the 500-entry cap are hard limits rather than UI suggestions. Offline reads come from Firestore's persistent cache and claims queue until reconnect. Print produces a paper sign-up sheet with blank lines for walk-ups.

comfortDefects.issue: The release/remove ✕ inside a claim chip measures 16×19px at default and 22×29px at Largest, the smallest interactive thing in the app, and it is the 'change my mind' path the research calls table stakes.

comfortDefects.issue: The availability figure, the single fact a participant came for, is .82rem (13.12px), below the system's 15px instructional floor.
'Full' is rendered in --pos green, the system's success colour.

comfortDefects.issue: .badge is .72rem (11.5px), smaller than --t-micro, which the system reserves for uppercase labels, and .banner is .88rem (14.1px) for sentences about locking and offline state.

comfortDefects.issue: The theme dots are 34×34 and .wkdays labels 33px tall; the ✎ edit is 37×36 and the .seg buttons 38px, all under the 44px floor at every comfort setting.

comfortDefects.issue: Selection state on the theme dots rests on a box-shadow ring plus colour alone, no tick, no aria-pressed, which the design system explicitly forbids for option groups.

comfortDefects.issue: The base's .trust stamp is unused, the privacy promise is grey footer prose, which the design system says users do not believe, and .empty is unused, so every empty state is a bare .hint paragraph.

comfortDefects.issue: SWS.saved() and the base's [data-saved-flag] are both unused; a successful slot save produces no feedback at all.
The QR canvas is a fixed 300×300 with the module grid computed from Math.floor(size/(count+8)), so at Largest text the dialog scales around a QR that does not.
comfortDefects.fix: Size the canvas from a rem value and redraw on the comfort change.

navigationDefects.issue: The Manage <details> is rebuilt with no open attribute on every redraw, so it closes on every mode switch, every add, every save, and on every remote claim, because Firestore snapshots drive drawBoard(). Measured: open true→false on one segment click; 102 redraws during one bulk add.
navigationDefects.fix: Persist details.open (and addMode) across redraws; better, stop replacing <main>.

navigationDefects.issue: Every slot opens its own onSnapshot whose callback calls drawBoard(), so a 60-slot sheet re-renders the whole page 73 times in six seconds.
navigationDefects.fix: Coalesce claim snapshots into one debounced render, and patch only the slot that changed.

navigationDefects.issue: A remote change destroys anything the current user has typed and throws focus to <body>, measured: a 29-character half-typed note wiped and the name field re-seeded from localStorage when an unrelated slot was renamed elsewhere.
navigationDefects.fix: Preserve field values and focus across a redraw, or never rebuild a subtree containing focus.

navigationDefects.issue: The claim dialog closes before the write resolves (53ms measured), so there is no progress state and a failed claim strands its typed note in a closed dialog that is blanked on next open.
navigationDefects.fix: Keep the dialog open with the button disabled until the promise settles.

navigationDefects.issue: A deleted board leaves a fully live-looking sheet on screen forever, because watchBoard passes null and drawBoard() early-returns.
navigationDefects.fix: Render the same 'this sheet is gone' card used for an unresolvable code (app.js:177-180).

navigationDefects.issue: No undo anywhere; four native confirm() dialogs instead, while window.SWS.undo is loaded and never called. Deleting a spot with signups is permanent and invisible to the people who signed up.

navigationDefects.issue: The current view is not fully in the URL: the add mode, the open/closed state of Manage and the scroll position all reset. Back from a board goes to home, which is correct, but there is no deep link to the owner console.

navigationDefects.issue: 'Your sheets' offers only Open, no fill count, no date, no delete, no duplicate, no archive, and deleting a sheet requires opening it and expanding Manage.

audit.printSupport: One real paper path, and it is good. The app print block (index.html:1319-1325) hides header.app, details.manage, every .btn, .noprint, #toast and footer.colophon, flattens section.card to borderless 4px rows, and reveals .printonly. app.js:327 prints a '________________' chip for every unclaimed place, so the sheet works as a real walk-up sign-up on a noticeboard, the research's 'compete with paper rather than against it', shipped. Verified by generating an A4 PDF from a live five-spot sheet with four claims: one page, title, description, 'x of y spots filled', every spot with its claimed names and notes, nine blank places, no chrome, no buttons, no share card. What is missing is the return path: no date, no share code, no URL, no QR, so nobody reading the paper can reach the live sheet. What is present and unwanted: the 'you run this' badge (app.js:240) and the Extras empty-state line '“I'll also bring lemonade!”, anything that isn't a listed spot goes here.' (app.js:365), which is a tonal misfire in ink on a bereavement meal train. The blank pills measure ~115px, short for a handwritten name. The .fillbar prints as a solid accent bar that disappears when the browser prints with background graphics off, leaving the numeric summary as the only signal, which is fine. Non-Latin names could not be verified here: this container has zero CJK fonts installed, so the tofu in the generated PDF is an environment artifact rather than an app defect, and unlike a pdf-lib path this one hands the glyphs to the OS.
riskyToRestyle: main#view is a live region that drawBoard() replaces on every Firestore snapshot. Any CSS transition, :focus-within rule or scroll anchoring attached to its children will fire or be destroyed continuously, measured at 73 replacements in six seconds on a 60-slot sheet.

applyTheme() writes --accent as an inline style on <html> (app.js:221), which beats every stylesheet rule including the comfort settings. Anything restyled in terms of --accent will change colour when an organizer picks a theme, and anything in terms of --accent-fill will not, that split is the current bug and it has to be resolved before either token is used more widely.

The bare `dialog{}` override at index.html:1313 also matches #swsPrefs. The comfort panel's own rules are scoped by ID and currently win, but any added specificity here reaches the shared panel in all 23 apps.
The app layer redefines .warn (index.html:1288), a base component. Restyling either one silently changes the other, and the app's error copy currently inherits the base's amber box with red text.

.chip does four jobs, a claimed name, your own claim, the printed blank line, and the base pill used elsewhere. Sizing it up to fix the 16px release ✕ also widens the printed blanks and every name pill; they need separate variants.

`.wkdays input{display:none}` is load-bearing for the current visual: the label uses :has(input:checked) for its selected state. Clipping the input instead (the correct fix) keeps :has working but exposes a focus ring that has to be styled on the label.
.printonly/.noprint are applied from JS on individual elements (app.js:253, 285, 307, 315, 327, 330, 382, 391), not only in CSS, so changing what prints means editing app.js, not the stylesheet.

The QR canvas is drawn at a fixed 300px with the cell size floored from the module count; changing #qrBox's box model or the canvas attributes without re-running showQR() produces a blurry or mis-quiet-zoned code.

vendor-qrcode.js is a classic script defining a global qrcode(), loaded before app.js and precached by sw.js; deferring it or converting it to a module breaks the QR path and the offline promise together.

sw.js precaches the three gstatic Firebase module URLs by exact version (12.17.1, matching the importmap at index.html:20-28). Changing the SDK version in one place without the other leaves an app serving a stale module from cache.

firestore.rules is the enforcement layer for every cap the UI shows. Any change to claim, entry or counter shape in data.js must be mirrored there and re-run through `npm run test:rules` (66-case matrix), the UI cannot loosen a limit on its own, and a mismatch surfaces to the user as the generic 'That didn't go through' toast.
